name: Chapter 1: Introduction to financial statements and their analysis

questions.text: Which set of functions is explicitly attributed to financial statements in the introductory lecture?

options.a: Human resources, logistics, and procurement
options.b: Information, profit and tax, and documentation
options.c: Product development, pricing, and distribution
options.d: Marketing, advertising, and investor relations

questions.text: Why do creditors use financial statements?

options.a: To replace all contractual loan agreements
options.b: To assess the protection of their claims and the firm's ability to meet obligations
options.c: To determine the firm's advertising slogan
options.d: To guarantee the future market value of shares

questions.text: Which is a primary information function of financial statements?

options.a: Eliminating the need for business strategy
options.b: Ensuring that every investment is profitable
options.c: Determining the exact market price of all assets
options.d: Helping investors and management make decisions

questions.text: Why is documentation important to financial reporting?

options.a: It makes the firm's competitive environment irrelevant
options.b: It guarantees a positive cash balance
options.c: It replaces the need for audit evidence
options.d: It provides a basis for accountability and capital preservation

questions.text: Which item belongs to the complete set of IFRS financial statements presented in the lecture?

options.a: Statement of changes in shareholders' equity
options.b: Employee training budget
options.c: Marketing performance statement
options.d: Customer satisfaction statement

questions.text: What does the balance sheet fundamentally describe?

options.a: Only cash received during a financial year
options.b: The exact market price of the firm over a year
options.c: Only the company's revenues and expenses
options.d: The assets and claims on those assets at a specific date

questions.text: Which accounting identity must hold on the balance sheet?

options.a: Assets = Liabilities + Shareholders' equity
options.b: Assets = Revenue - Expenses
options.c: Equity = Revenue + Expenses
options.d: Liabilities = Assets + Shareholders' equity

questions.text: What is shareholders' equity conceptually?

options.a: All payments owed to suppliers
options.b: The residual interest in assets after deducting liabilities
options.c: The total market value of outstanding bonds
options.d: The amount of cash held in the bank

questions.text: An economic resource expected to generate future economic benefits is best classified as what?

options.a: A dividend
options.b: An ownership distribution
options.c: An asset
options.d: An expense in all circumstances

questions.text: A firm's obligation to transfer economic resources to parties other than owners is generally a what?

options.a: Liability
options.b: Retained earning
options.c: Operating revenue
options.d: Share issue

questions.text: Which financial statement reports revenues less expenses over a reporting period?

options.a: The statement of changes in equity alone
options.b: The notes section alone
options.c: The balance sheet
options.d: The income statement

questions.text: Which statement groups cash flows by operating, investing, and financing activities?

options.a: Income statement
options.b: Cash flow statement
options.c: Statement of shareholders' equity
options.d: Balance sheet

questions.text: Which equation describes the change in cash as presented in the lecture?

options.a: Net income + Dividends
options.b: Operating cash flow + Investing cash flow + Financing cash flow
options.c: Assets - Liabilities
options.d: Revenue - Cost of goods sold

questions.text: What does contributed capital primarily represent?

options.a: Accumulated profits retained since incorporation
options.b: Amounts invested by shareholders through share issues
options.c: Unrealized foreign-currency movements only
options.d: Accounts payable arising from credit purchases

questions.text: How are retained earnings generally determined?

options.a: Cumulative net income less cumulative distributions of dividends
options.b: Total assets less financial liabilities
options.c: Cash balance less total debt
options.d: Revenue less purchases of property

questions.text: What is other comprehensive income (OCI) used for?

options.a: Reporting certain gains and losses outside net income
options.b: Recording every dividend paid as income
options.c: Reporting all cash receipts from customers
options.d: Recording the carrying value of all liabilities

questions.text: How is total comprehensive income related to net income?

options.a: Total comprehensive income = Net income - Total assets
options.b: Total comprehensive income = Assets - Liabilities
options.c: Total comprehensive income = Net income + Other comprehensive income
options.d: Total comprehensive income = Revenue + Cash flow

questions.text: According to the lecture, what is net payout to shareholders?

options.a: Assets - Current liabilities
options.b: Net income + Other comprehensive income
options.c: Share issues + Borrowings
options.d: Dividends + Share repurchases - Share issues

questions.text: How does a share repurchase affect the net payout measure, all else equal?

options.a: It reduces net payout to shareholders
options.b: It increases net payout to shareholders
options.c: It leaves net payout unchanged by definition
options.d: It is classified as other comprehensive income

questions.text: How does issuing new shares affect net payout, all else equal?

options.a: It creates an operating expense
options.b: It automatically increases retained earnings
options.c: It reduces net payout to shareholders
options.d: It increases net payout to shareholders

questions.text: Which relationship describes changes in equity in the lecture?

options.a: Ending equity = Beginning debt + Interest expense
options.b: Ending equity = Beginning equity + Comprehensive income - Net payout
options.c: Ending equity = Cash receipts - Cash payments
options.d: Ending equity = Revenue + Total assets

questions.text: What is a central reason equity investors analyze financial statements?

options.a: To calculate only a firm's tax liability
options.b: To determine customs tariffs
options.c: To evaluate investments and management performance
options.d: To set the legal retirement age

questions.text: What is a central reason debt investors analyze financial statements?

options.a: To assess default risk and possible covenant violations
options.b: To determine the dividend on all ordinary shares
options.c: To guarantee a capital gain from bonds
options.d: To replace credit ratings with employee data

questions.text: Which user is especially concerned with security of supply?

options.a: Customers
options.b: Only incumbent directors
options.c: Only bond underwriters
options.d: Only tax authorities

questions.text: Which user would most directly analyze financial statements for employment security and remuneration?

options.a: Potential customers only
options.b: Employees
options.c: Warehouse contractors only
options.d: Competing advertising agencies

questions.text: What is financial statement analysis in the lecture's demand-side framework?

options.a: A substitute for understanding business operations
options.b: A method for extracting information to answer users' questions about a firm
options.c: A process used only to prepare tax returns
options.d: A method for ensuring that accounting profits equal cash

questions.text: In the firm's investment cycle, what is the role of the company?

options.a: It deploys capital in activities that may add or destroy value
options.b: It guarantees investors a fixed return
options.c: It fixes the price of all traded securities
options.d: It only transfers securities among investors

questions.text: What distinguishes a secondary-market share purchase from a new share issue?

options.a: Neither transaction can change shareholders' positions
options.b: Both always create new shares and inject cash into the firm
options.c: A secondary-market purchase transfers ownership between investors, whereas a new issue raises funds for the firm
options.d: Only secondary-market transactions affect ownership

questions.text: Why might debtholders and shareholders disagree over profit distributions?

options.a: Profit distributions increase creditors' collateral without exception
options.b: Creditors always want dividends paid immediately
options.c: Dividends can reduce assets available to satisfy creditors' claims
options.d: Shareholders generally prefer more creditor protection over dividends

questions.text: Why do debtholders often prefer the firm to retain a sufficient equity cushion?

options.a: Equity holders must repay every bond personally
options.b: Retained equity legally eliminates all default risk
options.c: Equity absorbs losses before debt claims are affected
options.d: Higher equity necessarily raises borrowing costs

questions.text: What must an analyst understand before interpreting reported financial performance?

options.a: Only the latest share price
options.b: Only the total pages in the annual report
options.c: The firm's business model and competitive environment
options.d: Only the firm's legal name

questions.text: Which question is central when linking business strategy to valuation?

options.a: Can all qualitative factors be ignored?
options.b: Are competitors necessarily unprofitable?
options.c: How many fonts appear in the annual report?
options.d: How durable is the firm's competitive advantage?

questions.text: Why are financial statements useful when analyzing qualitative economic factors?

options.a: They provide a quantitative lens on business activity and performance
options.b: They fully disclose every intangible capability
options.c: They prove all strategic claims made by management
options.d: They eliminate the need for sector comparison

questions.text: Which three frameworks are introduced for business-environment analysis?

options.a: CAPM, Black-Scholes, and duration
options.b: FIFO, LIFO, and weighted average
options.c: Porter's value chain, Porter's five forces, and SWOT
options.d: DuPont, Altman Z-score, and free cash flow

questions.text: What does Porter's value chain emphasize?

options.a: Only external political risk
options.b: Only the relationship between assets and liabilities
options.c: How primary and support activities together generate value and affect cost
options.d: Only how debt is priced on capital markets

questions.text: Which is a primary activity in Porter's value chain?

options.a: Procurement
options.b: Outbound logistics
options.c: Human resource management
options.d: Firm infrastructure

questions.text: Which is a support activity in Porter's value chain?

options.a: Inbound logistics
options.b: Marketing and sales
options.c: After-sales service
options.d: Technology development

questions.text: In Porter's five-forces analysis, what tends to happen when buyers have strong bargaining power?

options.a: Suppliers automatically lose all bargaining power
options.b: Threat of substitution disappears
options.c: Industry rivalry ceases
options.d: They can demand lower prices or other concessions

questions.text: What is the likely effect of stronger supplier bargaining power?

options.a: Higher input prices or less favorable terms for firms
options.b: Guaranteed growth in customer demand
options.c: Lower cost of inputs in all cases
options.d: No change to industry profitability under any circumstances

questions.text: Why does the threat of substitutes matter for profitability?

options.a: Substitutes always increase incumbent monopoly power
options.b: Substitutes never affect pricing
options.c: Substitutes are identical to potential new entrants
options.d: Substitutes constrain the prices that existing firms can charge

questions.text: What is the typical effect of barriers to entry?

options.a: They guarantee superior management quality
options.b: They automatically eliminate industry rivalry
options.c: They reduce the threat posed by prospective entrants
options.d: They increase the number of new competitors

questions.text: Which dimensions are internal in a SWOT analysis?

options.a: Opportunities and weaknesses
options.b: Opportunities and threats
options.c: Threats and strengths
options.d: Strengths and weaknesses

questions.text: Which dimensions are external in a SWOT analysis?

options.a: Weaknesses and capabilities
options.b: Opportunities and threats
options.c: Strengths and opportunities
options.d: Strengths and weaknesses

questions.text: A newly introduced environmental regulation that raises compliance costs is most naturally classified as which SWOT dimension?

options.a: An internal weakness by definition
options.b: An internal opportunity by definition
options.c: An internal strength
options.d: An external threat

questions.text: A proprietary manufacturing capability that rivals struggle to replicate is most naturally classified as which SWOT dimension?

options.a: An internal strength
options.b: An external threat
options.c: An external opportunity
options.d: An internal weakness

questions.text: Why should cross-company comparisons consider competitive strategy?

options.a: Ratios completely adjust for differences in business models
options.b: Different business models can create fundamentally different accounting patterns and ratios
options.c: Competitive strategy has no connection to assets
options.d: All firms in an industry must have identical margins

questions.text: A creditor is analyzing a company that plans a very large dividend. Which concern most directly follows from the conflict identified in the lecture?

options.a: The distribution necessarily increases interest coverage
options.b: The distribution must increase the company's total liabilities by the dividend amount forever
options.c: The distribution ensures that shareholder and creditor objectives fully coincide
options.d: The distribution may reduce the assets available to repay the creditor

questions.text: A business expands sales rapidly but faces new substitutes and aggressive entrants. Which analytical conclusion is most defensible?

options.a: Threats from substitutes are internal strengths under SWOT
options.b: Revenue growth alone proves sustainable future margins
options.c: Strong current revenue growth may not represent durable competitive advantage
options.d: Porter's forces matter only when current profits are negative

questions.text: A company controls a highly productive factory, but lenders have contractual claims against it. Which distinction is accurate?

options.a: The factory and the lender claims are both equity
options.b: The factory is a liability because creditors may have claims on it
options.c: The factory is an asset; lenders' contractual claims are liabilities
options.d: The lender claims are assets because they finance operations

questions.text: A firm reports net income of 100, OCI of -20, dividends of 30, share repurchases of 10, and new share issues of 5. Which is its total comprehensive income?
An investor sees a profit increase without knowing whether competitors copied the firm's technology. What is the analytical gap?

options.a: Persistence of competitive advantage has not been assessed
options.b: Profit growth proves supplier power is zero
options.c: The balance sheet equation has been violated
options.d: The statement of cash flows is necessarily incorrect

questions.text: Which analyst question best connects Porter's value chain to reported profit margins?

options.a: Does every inventory item have a market price above cost?
options.b: Did the firm's shareholders buy shares in the secondary market?
options.c: Does its auditor use the same font as peers?
options.d: Are improvements in production and logistics reducing costs per unit of output?
